newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Rescuers find survivor in flattened Karachi block.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers find survivor in flattened Karachi block.

text.p: Rescue workers said on Friday they had found an injured man after giving up hope of finding more survivors from a collapsed building in Karachi.

"One barely alive labourer was pulled out of the debris last night, bringing the total number of survivors to 10, while a total of 11 dead were recovered in the rescue operation that started on Wednesday," a fire brigade official told Reuters.
He said the authorities, certain that no-one dead or alive remained in the rubble of the four-storey Faiza Heights block of flats, halted the search at six a.m. (0100 GMT) on Friday.
The official said the rescue of the critically injured man seemed a miracle as no-one had expected to find more survivors.

Rescue workers said initially up to 45 labourers could have been inside the building when it pancaked to the ground on Wednesday afternoon. By Thursday night they believed that 22 had been inside, of whom 16 were accounted for. Officials said on Friday they were now convinced only 21 people had been buried.
Officials have blamed the collapse of the almost-completed block on the use of poor building materials.
Police said the project supervisor had been arrested and they were searching for the architect, engineers and builders, against whom murder charges have been prepared.
